data.value: "If I have seen further, it is by standing upon the shoulders of giants"
data.comment: A famous quotation (Isaac Newton).

data.name: About_History1
data.value: Jack and Felix have done some great work but the originals use of a remote service to translate between image formats was an issue and the Port just wasn't proving stable enough for my needs. I really needed the ability to save projects, nest results and individual sheet placements, the ability to seed subsequent nests with the results of prior nests and the ability to edit placements - to slip that last piece in to the gaps on the sheet that the algorithm just wasn't finding.
data.comment: History written by the DeepNestSharp author, in the first person.

data.name: About_History2
data.value: Felix was keen to keep true to the original DeepNest code in DeepNestPort...

data.name: About_History3
data.value: ...so DeepNestSharp was born. It completely rebuilds the UI using WPF on Net.Core and is a huge refactor which has paid some dividends but also introduced some compromises and issues, some of which may still be outstanding... let me know.

data.name: About_Intro
data.value: SheetNest is a fork of DeepNestSharp, adding a GPU / raster nesting engine, an industrial production plan with grouped-layout DXF export, and a streamlined operator UI. MIT licensed; full lineage below.

data.name: About_MinkowskiExample
data.comment: Translate only the first word; the rest is a command.

data.name: About_MinkowskiIntro
data.value: Included are a set of minkowski.dlls that work on various Windows setups I have; AnyCpu, x86 and x64; but if you want to use the DllImport you'll likely need to build the dlls for your own setup. A lot of work has been done to ensure the native code is substitutable; and it is close but it's still experimental. Works for me, YMMV.

data.name: About_MinkowskiStep1
data.value: 1. Replace [boost_1.76_path]with your real BOOST (1.76+) path in compile.bat
data.comment: Keep [boost_1.76_path] and compile.bat as written.

data.name: About_MinkowskiStep2
data.value: 2. Run compile.bat using Developer Command Prompt for Visual Studio

data.name: About_MinkowskiVisualStudio
data.value: If you're running in Visual Studio DeepNestLib.CiTests has a PostBuild task to copy the DLLs from there for you. Otherwise make sure the appropriate DLLs get to the DeepNestSharp.exe folder. Note there's preprocessor directives to pick the right dll dependent on which Arch you're running.

data.name: Offcut_Auto
data.comment: Caption under a picture card about 96 px wide.

data.name: Offcut_AutoTip
data.value: Weighs End, Side and Both against the layout the nest produced and keeps whichever frees the most material.
data.comment: End, Side and Both are the other three cards.

data.name: Offcut_Both
data.comment: Caption under a picture card about 96 px wide.

data.name: Offcut_BothTip
data.value: When the nest left room on both sides, the leftover comes away as two rectangles (guillotine cuts, so no cut ever splits a remnant in two).

data.name: Offcut_EdgeOverlapFormat
data.comment: {0} is the unit symbol, in or mm.

data.name: Offcut_EdgeOverlapTip
data.value: How far the cut runs PAST the sheet edge at each end, so the remnant comes away instead of hanging on by a bridge at the corners. 0 = flush with the edge.

data.name: Offcut_Enable
data.value: Cut the leftover off as a rectangular offcut
data.comment: Check box.

data.name: Offcut_EnableTip
data.value: Measures the free area the nest left on the last sheet and adds a cut line so it comes away as a reusable rectangle. It never moves a part: the nest is already finished by the time this is worked out, so turning it on cannot change where anything is placed.

data.name: Offcut_End
data.comment: Caption under a picture card about 96 px wide.

data.name: Offcut_EndTip
data.value: A full strip at the end of the sheet's long side: the classic remnant.

data.name: Offcut_MaxXFormat
data.comment: {0} is the unit symbol, in or mm.

data.name: Offcut_MaxXTip
data.value: Widest remnant still worth cutting off. Bigger than this and it is not a remnant but very nearly a sheet, so nothing is cut and the sheet is kept whole. 0 = no limit.

data.name: Offcut_MaxYFormat
data.comment: {0} is the unit symbol, in or mm.

data.name: Offcut_MaxYTip
data.value: Tallest remnant still worth cutting off. 0 = no limit.

data.name: Offcut_MinXFormat
data.comment: {0} is the unit symbol, in or mm.

data.name: Offcut_MinXTip
data.value: Narrowest remnant worth separating. Below this the sheet is left uncut. 0 = automatic (5% of the sheet's side).

data.name: Offcut_MinYFormat
data.comment: {0} is the unit symbol, in or mm.

data.name: Offcut_MinYTip
data.value: Shortest remnant worth separating. 0 = automatic (5% of the sheet's side).

data.name: Offcut_RemnantPosition
data.comment: Heading over four picture cards.

data.name: Offcut_ResetDefaultsTip
data.value: Puts the six numbers above back to the recommended figures for this drawing's units. The remnant position and the enable tick are left alone.

data.name: Rotation_0And180Tip
data.value: 0° and 180°: respects material grain but can flip.

data.name: Rotation_45Steps
data.comment: Rotation option: eight angles 45 degrees apart. Very small button.

data.name: Rotation_45StepsTip
data.value: Eight orientations, 45° apart. The job setting offers this too, and without it here a part could not be shown what it was really set to.

data.name: Rotation_4Way
data.comment: Rotation option: 0, 90, 180 and 270 degrees. Very small button.

data.name: Rotation_4WayTip
data.value: All four square orientations (0 / 90 / 180 / 270°). The safe first choice on square and L shaped parts: it usually beats free rotation on those, and always costs less to search.

data.name: Rotation_90Only
data.comment: Rotation option. Very small button.

data.name: Rotation_90OnlyTip
data.value: Only 90°, so the part is always turned once.

data.name: Rotation_AsDrawn
data.comment: Rotation option: only 0 degrees. Very small button.

data.name: Rotation_AsDrawnTip
data.value: Only 0°, so the part stays exactly as drawn (respects grain).

data.name: Rotation_Free
data.comment: Rotation option: any angle. Very small button.

data.name: Rotation_FreeTip
data.value: Any angle, and NOT automatically the tightest. It wins on parts with slanted or curved edges, and loses on square or L shaped ones, which interlock exactly at right angles and gain nothing from being tilted. Measured on two real jobs: 84.3% of the block filled against 4-way's 81.6% on one, and 69.6% against 73.2% on the other. Costs about twice the search. Ignores grain.
data.comment: "4-way" is the Rotation_4Way option.

data.name: Rotation_JobDefault
data.comment: Rotation option: the part follows the job's setting. Very small button.

data.name: Rotation_JobDefaultTip
data.value: Whatever the job is set to, under Settings > Advanced Settings. Change it there and this part follows.

data.name: Viewer_EditNestTip
data.value: Manual nesting: click a part to select it, drag to move, rotate with the buttons. Dragging may leave a part on top of another while you rearrange: it turns red, and the export refuses until nothing is red. Hold Alt as you drop to slide it against its neighbour instead. The arrow keys will not push a properly placed part into a neighbour, but they do move one that is already red, so you can walk it clear. Edits apply to every copy of this layout and flow into the DXF export.
